rule_text: There is a Mother and a Child.
The Child can have one active Need at a time.
The user creates or triggers a Need.
A Need has a name.
Example Need names include milk, water, food, toy, sleep.
The Need name matters.
Mother can only satisfy a Need if she has a matching rule for it.
Every Need has a dissatisfaction variable.
Dissatisfaction starts at 0 when the Need begins.
Dissatisfaction rises slowly over time.
The rise speed is programmable per Need.
Default rise speed should be 1 point per minute.
The Need has an action threshold.
The threshold is programmable.
When dissatisfaction is below the threshold, the Child waits.
When dissatisfaction rises above the threshold, the Child must act.
The Child’s only action is to say/print words to the screen.
The Child does not point, move, grab, or gesture yet.
The Child says words from a selected word list.
Words are said at random gaps between 0 and 3 seconds.
The Child starts with a base list of 70 early-child words.
The 70-word base list includes words like mama, dada, milk, more, water, food, toy, sleep.
The base 70-word list is not always used first.
The base 70-word list is the final fallback.
The Mother has her own rules.
A Mother rule says: for this Need, if the Child says this word, give this thing.
Example rule: Need milk, trigger word milk, give item milk.
Mother listens automatically.
If the Child says the correct trigger word for the active Need, Mother detects it.
The correct word does not instantly satisfy the Need.
Mother waits a random delay.
Default delay is 9 to 12 seconds.
During this delay, Mother is in a pending/preparing state.
Mother must not schedule duplicate deliveries for the same Need.
After the delay, Mother says “ok”.
Mother then gives the requested item.
Only after Mother says “ok” and gives the item does dissatisfaction reset.
Dissatisfaction resets immediately to 0.
The reset is the Child’s proof that something worked.
The Child is not directly told which exact word worked.
The Child only knows that the recent words before “ok” may have worked.
When dissatisfaction resets, the Child saves the words spoken in that round.
It saves up to the last 20 words.
If fewer than 20 words were spoken, it saves all of them.
The saved words become a plausible approach for that Need.
Each Need has its own active memory.
milk has its own active memory.
water has its own active memory.
food has its own active memory.
toy has its own active memory.
A Need’s active memory is the newest successful word list for that Need.
Every successful saved list is also kept in history.
Saved lists are kept chronologically.
Older lists are not deleted.
Re-triggering the same Need uses that Need’s active memory first.
Example: if milk has learned milk, then next time milk is needed, Child uses milk memory first.
Each successful round may shrink the active memory.
Over time, the Child should naturally whittle a broad list down toward useful word or words, but this must not be artificially forced or rigged.
If a Need is new and has no active memory, the Child must not jump straight to the base 70-word list.
For a new Need, the Child first tries other known Needs’ active memories.
Example: new Need juice may first try the active memory for milk.
Then it may try the active memory for water.
Then it may try the active memory for food.
If active memories do not work, the Child walks backward through older saved lists.
It walks back one generation at a time.
Search depth 0 means current active memories.
Search depth 1 means previous saved lists.
Search depth 2 means older saved lists.
This continues across all known Need memories.
Only after all known memories fail does the Child use the base 70-word list.
If a borrowed list works for a new Need, the new Need gets its own memory.
Example: if a borrowed list helps satisfy juice, then juice now gets its own active memory.
From then on, juice uses its own active memory first.
The Child’s brain workings must be visible on screen.
The UI must show the current Need.
The UI must show dissatisfaction level.
The UI must show rise rate.
The UI must show action threshold.
The UI must show Child mode: waiting, rising, speaking, pending/preparing, satisfied, learning saved.
The UI must show the current word source.
The UI must show whether the source is own memory, borrowed memory, archived memory, or base list.
The UI must show fallback depth.
The UI must show which Need memory is being borrowed.
The UI must show words spoken this round.
The UI must show Mother status.
The UI must show whether Mother has a matching rule for the active Need.
The UI must warn if no Mother rule can satisfy the current Need.
The UI must show pending Mother delivery.
The UI must show Mother saying “ok”.
The UI must show the item given.
The UI must show memory saved after reset.
The UI must show active memory for the current Need.
The UI must show saved list history.
The UI must show all Need memories.
The UI must show the Brain/Event Log.
The Brain/Event Log must record real events, not fake text.
localStorage should persist the Child’s learned memory.
There must be a way to clear/reset learned memory.
Clearing memory must not delete the base 70-word list.
Clearing memory must not delete default Mother rules.
Manual Mother controls may exist, but only as clearly marked test controls.
Normal learning must work automatically without pressing manual fulfil.
The app must make it obvious when the Child is yelling into the void because no Mother rule matches the Need.
The goal is not just word guessing.
The goal is visible learning through Need → dissatisfaction → speech → Mother response → reset → memory.
For a known Need with its own active memory, exhausting that memory must not repeat words; it must wait with no unused words remaining.
For a known Need with its own active memory, exhausting the active memory must not make the Child jump to Base.
For a known Need with its own active memory, exhausting the active memory must not make the Child fall back to older archived lists.
Older saved lists for a known Need are historical records, not active behavior, unless a future regression/confusion mode is explicitly introduced.
During Mother pending/preparing delay, the Child must keep speaking while unused words remain in the current source, then wait without repeating when exhausted.
During Mother pending/preparing delay, dissatisfaction must continue until Mother says ok and gives the item.
The final spoken word should remain visible in the Child Speech Stream after satisfaction.
The event log should clearly show ordering, such as Newest First or Oldest First.
The event log should make latest events easy to see, by auto-scroll or Jump to latest.
Memory-save log entries should show exact saved words and saved count.
The current accepted UX is: user may click Begin Need first, then Start. Begin Need does not need to auto-start for now.
During a single Need run, the Child must not repeat a word already spoken in that run, including across fallback sources.
